svg.aria-label: How to write ಘ: 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing ಘ
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಘ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-gha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಘ, 61 frames, 6.1 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-gha.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation writes ಘ in five pen-down runs: from the inner tip of the curl the pen winds up and round to the left, runs along the base, rises into the middle point, drops round the right lobe, climbs the right side and carries on up the middle arm to its tip (frames 0–16); after a lift it starts again at the foot of the middle arm and rounds the right arm, curling in at its top (frames 19–24); after a second lift, the top bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 28–38); after a third lift, the dot in the middle (frames 43–44); after a fourth lift, the tail below the point, drawn downward (frames 48–49). The frames were read from a mirror copy that matches the Commons file's listed pixel size (225×210); the listing gives no byte size or frame count to compare. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the dot is a filled disc, drawn as a small closed loop inside it, and the tail is a short tapered bar. These runs stage the letter one part at a time; they are not a count of how often fluent writers lift the pen, and no native writers' pen data for Kannada was available. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ಘ, each by a different Amazon Mechanical Turk worker copying a printed exemplar online. They are non-native copyists, not native writers; where the same dataset can be set beside native writers' pen data (HP Labs India's Devanagari and Bangla sets), the copyists use more strokes than those writers, so their counts are read here only as a ceiling on native lifts, and only counts and shares are cited. Even under that ceiling, 65% of them (13 of 20) draw ಘ in four strokes; 15% (3 of 20) use the animation's five. Those counts say how many strokes, not where they break, so this learner path keeps every run's order, start and direction as a segment and joins only the middle arm to the right arm, coming back down the middle arm to its foot, so the pen lifts three times.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 10 movements
Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-gha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಘ, 61 frames, 6.1 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
